summary: The guest is best known publicly as a famous actor's girlfriend, and the dominant reaction is that they had no idea she was this funny — several say they only knew her name and now see her as a person in her own right. One comment notes the booking strategy out loud: they could never get the actor, so they got his girlfriend and it worked. A cluster asks to see the couple's moments and for the pair to make YouTube content together. The most substantial comment is a long, unsparing analysis of the relationship dynamic, arguing she has endured a partner who keeps her invisible and that she should manage her expectations about marriage — critical of him, sympathetic to her. Others encourage her to be more confident, sensing she was holding back out of deference to his fanbase.

audience_signals: Booking a hard-to-get star's partner is an effective substitute strategy: it delivers adjacent access and the audience recognises and applauds the manoeuvre
The channel measurably re-positions guests — viewers who knew her only as someone's girlfriend leave describing her as a personality, which is a benefit worth naming when pitching bookings
Even mid-tier episodes attract long-form relationship analysis, so the comment corpus is a usable source of audience attitudes about relationships generally, not just about the guests
Viewers detect when a guest is self-censoring for their partner's fanbase, so making a guest feel safe is visible in the output
